messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High gateway 502/504 spike detected for gw-edge-prod in us-west-2. error-rate: 7.8% (5m) :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: Paging @anya (oncall) :phone: — severity: P2, customers seeing failures: ~3.2k requests/min, latency p95 up from 120ms -> 450ms
anya: Acknowledged. jumping in. any obvious correlate in deployments?
kevin: no deploys in the last 30m. saw a config push to envoy-filter 2h ago but nothing recent
sara: looking at traces — sampling looks near zero for gw-edge today, spans missing for a large fraction of requests. trying trace index query now
leo: checking logs — most gateway logs show 502 without request_id header. seems like upstream proxy is dropping x-request-id for these requests
anya: ok that rings alarm bells. if request ids lost we can't tie logs->traces. that's the "observability gap" we need to fix asap
ops-bot: Metric snapshot: gw-edge upstream_502_count +420% in 5m, upstream_timeout_count +210%, trace_ingest_rate -95% relative to baseline
matt: any customer-facing impact? CSMs need numbers for notices
kevin: quick calc from router metrics: ~3.2k failed requests/min, approx 0.6% of total auth traffic but concentrated on some orgs hitting specific endpoints — raising to CSMs now
sara: sample query to traces: `service:gw-edge AND timestamp:now-1h` returned only 12 spans vs expected ~10k. sampler config maybe toggled off earlier today by infra job
anya: action plan: 1) increase trace sampling to 100% for gw-edge for 15m; 2) enable debug logging at proxy for header propagation; 3) temporary proxy filter to re-inject missing x-request-id if present in connection metadata; 4) route degraded traffic to fallback pool if 502 rate stays >5%
leo: can deploy the re-inject filter quickly? I have a small envoy filter snippet tested locally
leo: ```yaml
# envoy filter patch (temp)
- name: rekey-x-request-id
  apply_to: NETWORK_FILTER
  patch: |
    # inject x-request-id from connection metadata if header missing
    # temp stopgap, rollback after mitigation
```
kevin: rolling the filter in canary to 2 hosts in us-west-2 now via infra-cd: `infra-cd deploy gw-edge/filter-reinject --canary 2`
ops-bot: infra-cd: started deploy job 4621 (gw-edge/filter-reinject) — canary 2 hosts
anya: sara, once sampling is up can you validate traces start showing? also add a quick synthetic trace from curl to confirm propagation
sara: increasing sampling: `kubectl set env deployment/gw-edge TRACE_SAMPLING=1.0 -n prod` -> patch applied to gw-edge pods in us-west-2
sara: synthetic curl test: `curl -v -H "x-request-id: test-123" https://gw-edge-prod/api/health` -> response 200, header echoed back, logs: `req_id=test-123` appears in pod stdout
sara: trace ingest now shows more spans. ingestion at 62% of expected, still catching up
kevin: canary of filter returned no immediate errors. promoting to 20% of hosts now
ops-bot: deploy job 4621: promoted to 20% (4/20 hosts) — monitoring for 120s
anya: while we get visibility we should put in a traffic-level stopgap: add fallback routing to rpc-pool-v1 which is older but stable
leo: adding a route rule: `route /api -> weight: gw-edge:80, rpc-pool-v1:20` for 10m. applying now
ops-bot: route update submitted (change-id 8887)
matt: CSMs notified: initial message sent — telling affected customers we're investigating and may apply short reroutes. Will update with concrete timeline once we stabilize
kevin: after filter at 20% and sampling bump, 502 rate dropped to 3.1% in 2m. p95 latency trending down to 200ms
sara: traces are back, we can now correlate failures to a downstream auth service timing out at 2500ms for particular calls
anya: good find. mitigation: increase timeout/retry for auth calls temporarily and scale auth replicas by +2
leo: patching auth client: set `timeout=5s` -> rolling restart for gw-edge to pick up new client config
ops-bot: auth replicas scaled from 4 -> 8 in us-west-2 via autoscaler override
kevin: monitoring: auth error rate dropped, upstream 502s falling to 0.9% in last 5m
anya: next steps: 1) keep sampling at 100% for 30m to validate, 2) keep reinject filter for 1h then revert, 3) create follow-up postmortem for why request-id propagation broke and why sampler toggled off, 4) notify product/CS for possible customer comms
sara: capturing quick runbook edits: add a step to verify `x-request-id` propagation after proxy config changes, add automated check in CD job
matt: oncall handoff in 25m — @anya please add to the handoff note: current state stabilized, sampling 100%, reinject filter active, fallback route removed (was temporary), auth scaled, customers notified
anya: will include. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: NOTE: temporary debug logs enabled, retention limited to 1h. remember to disable to avoid bill shock
csm-bot: CSM update: initial ping sent to 5 affected enterprise customers; awaiting replies. will escalate to account leads if any report data loss
kevin: wrapping up CI: rolling back reinject filter in 55m unless we see regressions. opening ticket INFRA-3121 to track long-term fix for header propagation
anya: Closing loop: if anything spikes reopen this thread. otherwise will write up timeline and attach traces for postmortem. thanks team. :pray:
